observation.visible_scene: An indoor aquatic exhibit, likely a zoo or aquarium, featuring a large pool of blue water separated from viewers by a glass wall. The background consists of artificial white rock formations resembling ice or snow, with some enrichment objects like an orange raft and blue barrels visible near the edge. In the foreground, silhouetted against the bright tank, several visitors are watching; one person on the right is holding up a smartphone to record the scene. A polar bear is the central subject in the water.
visible_changes: The polar bear begins the clip floating leisurely on its back in the middle of the pool, with its paws raised out of the water.
Over the course of the clip, the bear rotates its body and transitions from a supine floating position to an upright swimming posture.
The bear swims steadily towards the glass barrier in the foreground, moving closer to the visitors.
As the bear approaches the glass, its reflection becomes visible on the underside of the water surface.
The visitor on the right maintains their position, holding their phone up to capture the bear's movement throughout the sequence.
outside_clip_unknowns: The specific motivation for the bear's change in behavior from floating to swimming.
What happens after the bear reaches the glass or interacts with the visitors.
The full extent of the exhibit beyond the visible frame boundaries.
uncertain_details: The exact species of the bear is inferred from appearance but not explicitly labeled in the visual data.
Whether the camera movement (slight zoom/pan) is intentional or handheld shake.
